metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies when AI wrote 'the vast majority' of the submission
domains.accountability_holder: The contributor submitting the pull request (must document their own AI use)

evidence.quote: If you use Generative AI to write the vast majority of your submission (e.g., agent-based or vibe coding) then you must document your use of AI in your pull request.

domains.reasoning: The 'Using AI' section names code contributions explicitly, requires disclosure of AI use in the PR (supervision level), and implicitly assigns the disclosure duty to the submitting contributor. The subsequent line about 'rigorous review process' is enforcement/QA, not an accountability statement, but the disclosure obligation itself is enough to name the contributor as answerable for declaring AI involvement.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md discusses code, feature requests, bug reports, translations and coding style but never mentions recorded meetings, calls, or notetaker/transcription bots.

domains.suggested_improvement: no AI rule for docs/artwork; no supervision or holder named
domains.reasoning: The Open Source Contribution Policy notes that contributions can include 'documentation and artistic works as appropriate to the project,' but the AI-specific 'Using AI' section only discusses code submissions and does not extend disclosure or supervision requirements to documentation, blog posts, or design assets.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The document references the Code of Conduct only in the context of limiting community access for violations; it never discusses AI tools being used to moderate issues, comments, or community behavior.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on whether reviewers may use AI tools
domains.reasoning: The statement 'All code submissions go through a rigorous review process regardless of the development workflow used' confirms a human review step exists but says nothing about whether maintainers/reviewers themselves may use AI tools to conduct that review, so it does not name or set a rule for AI-assisted review.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies specifically to 'agent-based or vibe coding' generating the vast majority of a submission
domains.accountability_holder: The contributor submitting the pull request

evidence.quote: If you use Generative AI to write the vast majority of your submission (e.g., agent-based or vibe coding) then you must document your use of AI in your pull request.

domains.reasoning: Agent-based ('agentic') coding is explicitly named as an example requiring disclosure, giving a supervision level (disclosure) and accountability holder (the contributor) for autonomous/agentic code generation specifically.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy/water/hardware footprint of AI
domains.reasoning: The document contains no discussion, positive or negative, of the environmental costs of AI tools; the 'Using AI' section is framed purely around disclosure and code quality, not resource concerns.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server/CI load or hardware cost from AI use
domains.reasoning: No text addresses strain on project infrastructure (CI runners, hosting, maintainer bandwidth costs) from AI-generated volume of contributions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on use of project/user data for AI training
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md never discusses whether project data, code, or user data may be used to train AI models; the licensing language in the Open Source Contribution Policy concerns code reuse/licensing generally, not AI training data.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: CONTRIBUTING.md addresses AI use narrowly and only for code submissions: it requires contributors to disclose when Generative AI (including agent-based/"vibe" coding) produced the vast majority of a PR's content, and states that all code still undergoes human review, but it is silent on notetaker bots, non-code content, moderation, AI-assisted review, environmental/infrastructure impact, and training data.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
